claim: Expression of NPRL2/TUSC4, a tumor-suppressor gene, is reduced in many cancers including NSCLC.
source: Expression of NPRL2/TUSC4, a tumor-suppressor gene, is reduced in many cancers including NSCLC.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction section.

claim: Restoration of NPRL2 induces DNA damage, apoptosis, and cell-cycle arrest.
source: Restoration of NPRL2 induces DNA damage, apoptosis, and cell-cycle arrest.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in the results section showing apoptosis induction and cell cycle arrest.

claim: NPRL2-treatment reduced lung metastases significantly in humanized mice.
source: NPRL2-treatment reduced lung metastases significantly, whereas pembrolizumab was ineffective.
evidence: Supported by bioluminescence imaging data showing tumor reduction in Figure 2.

claim: Pembrolizumab was ineffective in treating KRAS/STK11 mutant anti-PD1 resistant tumors.
source: NPRL2-treatment reduced lung metastases significantly, whereas pembrolizumab was ineffective.
evidence: Demonstrated by tumor growth data in Figure 2 showing no significant effect of pembrolizumab.

claim: Antitumor effect of NPRL2 was greater in humanized than non-humanized mice.
source: Antitumor effect was greater in humanized than non-humanized-mice.
evidence: Supported by comparative data in Figure 2H showing statistically significant difference (p=0.008).

claim: NPRL2 + pembrolizumab was not synergistic in KRAS/STK11mt/aPD1R tumors.
source: NPRL2 + pembrolizumab was not synergistic in KRAS/STK11mt/aPD1R tumors but was synergistic in KRASwt/aPD1S H1299.
evidence: Demonstrated by tumor growth data in Figure 2I-J showing no additional benefit of combination in A549 tumors.

claim: NPRL2 + pembrolizumab was synergistic in KRASwt/aPD1S H1299 tumors.
source: NPRL2 + pembrolizumab was not synergistic in KRAS/STK11mt/aPD1R tumors but was synergistic in KRASwt/aPD1S H1299.
evidence: Supported by tumor growth data in Figure 4D showing enhanced antitumor effect of combination treatment.

claim: NPRL2 showed a significant antitumor effect on KRASmt/aPD1R LLC2 syngeneic tumors.
source: NPRL2 also showed a significant antitumor effect on KRASmt/aPD1R LLC2 syngeneic-tumors.
evidence: Demonstrated by tumor growth curves in Figure 5B showing significant tumor reduction (p<0.005).

claim: NPRL2 treatment increased infiltration of human cytotoxic-T cells in the tumor microenvironment.
source: The antitumor effect was correlated with increased infiltration of human cytotoxic-T, HLA-DR+DC, CD11c+DC, and downregulation of myeloid and regulatory-T cells in TME.
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 3C showing increased CD8+ T cells (p<0.005).

claim: NPRL2 treatment increased infiltration of HLA-DR+ dendritic cells in the tumor microenvironment.
source: The antitumor effect was correlated with increased infiltration of human cytotoxic-T, HLA-DR+DC, CD11c+DC, and downregulation of myeloid and regulatory-T cells in TME.
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 3K showing increased HLA-DR+ DC (p<0.005).

claim: NPRL2 treatment downregulated myeloid-derived suppressor cells in the tumor microenvironment.
source: The antitumor effect was correlated with increased infiltration of human cytotoxic-T, HLA-DR+DC, CD11c+DC, and downregulation of myeloid and regulatory-T cells in TME.
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 3L showing decreased MDSC (p<0.0005).

claim: NPRL2 treatment downregulated regulatory T cells in the tumor microenvironment.
source: The antitumor effect was correlated with increased infiltration of human cytotoxic-T, HLA-DR+DC, CD11c+DC, and downregulation of myeloid and regulatory-T cells in TME.
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 3D showing decreased Treg (p<0.005).

claim: Antitumor effect of NPRL2 was abolished upon in-vivo depletion of CD8-T cells.
source: Antitumor effect was abolished upon in-vivo depletion of CD8-T, macrophages, and CD4-T cells whereas remained unaffected upon NK-cell depletion.
evidence: Demonstrated by tumor growth data in Figure 6D showing loss of antitumor effect when CD8+ T cells were depleted.

claim: Antitumor effect of NPRL2 was abolished upon in-vivo depletion of macrophages.
source: Antitumor effect was abolished upon in-vivo depletion of CD8-T, macrophages, and CD4-T cells whereas remained unaffected upon NK-cell depletion.
evidence: Demonstrated by tumor growth data in Figure 6F showing loss of antitumor effect when macrophages were depleted.

claim: Antitumor effect of NPRL2 was abolished upon in-vivo depletion of CD4-T cells.
source: Antitumor effect was abolished upon in-vivo depletion of CD8-T, macrophages, and CD4-T cells whereas remained unaffected upon NK-cell depletion.
evidence: Demonstrated by tumor growth data in Figure 6C showing reduced antitumor effect when CD4+ T cells were depleted.

claim: Antitumor effect of NPRL2 remained unaffected upon NK-cell depletion.
source: Antitumor effect was abolished upon in-vivo depletion of CD8-T, macrophages, and CD4-T cells whereas remained unaffected upon NK-cell depletion.
evidence: Demonstrated by tumor growth data in Figure 6E showing maintained antitumor effect when NK cells were depleted.

claim: IFNγ expression was significantly increased after NPRL2 treatment.
source: IFNγ, CD8b, and TBX21 associated with T-cell functions were significantly increased, whereas FOXP3, TGFB1/B2, and IL-10RA were strongly inhibited by NPRL2.
evidence: Supported by NanoString gene expression data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: CD8b expression was significantly increased after NPRL2 treatment.
source: IFNγ, CD8b, and TBX21 associated with T-cell functions were significantly increased, whereas FOXP3, TGFB1/B2, and IL-10RA were strongly inhibited by NPRL2.
evidence: Supported by NanoString gene expression data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: TBX21 expression was significantly increased after NPRL2 treatment.
source: IFNγ, CD8b, and TBX21 associated with T-cell functions were significantly increased, whereas FOXP3, TGFB1/B2, and IL-10RA were strongly inhibited by NPRL2.
evidence: Supported by NanoString gene expression data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: FOXP3 expression was strongly inhibited by NPRL2 treatment.
source: IFNγ, CD8b, and TBX21 associated with T-cell functions were significantly increased, whereas FOXP3, TGFB1/B2, and IL-10RA were strongly inhibited by NPRL2.
evidence: Supported by NanoString gene expression data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: TGFB1 expression was strongly inhibited by NPRL2 treatment.
source: IFNγ, CD8b, and TBX21 associated with T-cell functions were significantly increased, whereas FOXP3, TGFB1/B2, and IL-10RA were strongly inhibited by NPRL2.
evidence: Supported by NanoString gene expression data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: TGFB2 expression was strongly inhibited by NPRL2 treatment.
source: IFNγ, CD8b, and TBX21 associated with T-cell functions were significantly increased, whereas FOXP3, TGFB1/B2, and IL-10RA were strongly inhibited by NPRL2.
evidence: Supported by NanoString gene expression data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: IL-10RA expression was strongly inhibited by NPRL2 treatment.
source: IFNγ, CD8b, and TBX21 associated with T-cell functions were significantly increased, whereas FOXP3, TGFB1/B2, and IL-10RA were strongly inhibited by NPRL2.
evidence: Supported by NanoString gene expression data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: A list of T-cell co-inhibitory molecules was downregulated by NPRL2 treatment.
source: A list of T-cell co-inhibitory molecules was also downregulated.
evidence: Supported by NanoString gene expression data in Figure 7E showing downregulation of CTLA4, ICOS, LAG3, PDCD1, CD274, IDO1, PDCD1LG2, CD47, KLRB1.

claim: Restoration of NPRL2 exhibited significantly slower tumor growth in humanized mice.
source: Restoration of NPRL2 exhibited significantly slower tumor growth in humanized-mice, which was associated with increased presence of human cytotoxic-T, and DC and decreased percentage of Treg, MDSC, and TAM in TME.
evidence: Demonstrated by tumor growth curves in Figure 8C showing reduced tumor growth in H1299-NPRL2++/++ tumors.

claim: NPRL2-stable cells showed a substantial increase in colony-formation inhibition.
source: NPRL2-stable cells showed a substantial increase in colony-formation inhibition and heightened sensitivity to carboplatin.
evidence: Demonstrated by colony formation assay data in Figure 8O showing reduced colony formation in NPRL2 stable cells.

claim: NPRL2-stable cells showed heightened sensitivity to carboplatin.
source: NPRL2-stable cells showed a substantial increase in colony-formation inhibition and heightened sensitivity to carboplatin.
evidence: Demonstrated by apoptosis assay data in Figure 8Q showing increased apoptosis in NPRL2 stable cells treated with carboplatin.

claim: Stable-expression of NPRL2 resulted in the downregulation of MAPK signaling.
source: Stable-expression of NPRL2 resulted in the downregulation of MAPK and AKT-mTOR signaling.
evidence: Demonstrated by Western blot data in Figure 8S showing decreased phospho-ERK1/2 in NPRL2 stable cells.

claim: Stable-expression of NPRL2 resulted in the downregulation of AKT-mTOR signaling.
source: Stable-expression of NPRL2 resulted in the downregulation of MAPK and AKT-mTOR signaling.
evidence: Demonstrated by Western blot data in Figure 8S showing decreased phospho-AKT, phospho-mTOR, and downstream targets in NPRL2 stable cells.

claim: NPRL2 gene-therapy induces antitumor activity on KRAS/STK11mt/aPD1R tumors through DC-mediated antigen-presentation and cytotoxic immune-cell activation.
source: Taken-together, NPRL2 gene-therapy induces antitumor activity on KRAS/STK11mt/aPD1R tumors through DC-mediated antigen-presentation and cytotoxic immune-cell activation.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on multiple experimental findings including immune cell depletion studies and TME analysis.

claim: NPRL2 is located on chromosome 3p21.31 in a cluster with other tumor suppressor genes including TUSC2/FUS1.
source: NPRL2 (Nitrogen Permease Regulator-Like 2) is also known as TUSC4, a tumor suppressor gene, located on chromosome 3p21.31 in a cluster with other tumor suppressor genes including TUSC2/FUS1 (Kondo et al., 2001; Lerman and Minna, 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Reduced expression or deletion of NPRL2 was found in many cancers including lung, renal, colorectal, glioma, gastric, and hepatocellular carcinoma.
source: Reduced expression or deletion of NPRL2 was found in many cancers including lung, renal, colorectal, glioma, gastric, and hepatocellular carcinoma, and has been closely correlated with poor clinical outcomes (Liu et al., 2014; Pi et al., 2022; Huang et al., 2016; Tang et al., 2014; Otani et al., 2009; Senchenko et al., 2010; Zabarovsky et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with multiple supporting citations.

claim: Low expression of NPRL2 in distinct types of lung cancers was associated with cisplatin resistance.
source: We previously reported that low expression of NPRL2 in distinct types of lung cancers was associated with cisplatin resistance (Ueda et al., 2006) and restoration of NPRL2 in NPRL2 deficient cells overcomes cisplatin resistance through the activation of the DNA damage checkpoint pathway (Jayachandran et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations to previous work.

claim: Restoration of NPRL2 in NPRL2 deficient cells overcomes cisplatin resistance through the activation of the DNA damage checkpoint pathway.
source: We previously reported that low expression of NPRL2 in distinct types of lung cancers was associated with cisplatin resistance (Ueda et al., 2006) and restoration of NPRL2 in NPRL2 deficient cells overcomes cisplatin resistance through the activation of the DNA damage checkpoint pathway (Jayachandran et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: NPRL2 induces apoptosis by causing cell cycle arrest in G1 in cells with active p53.
source: NPRL2 induces apoptosis and DNA damage in cells with active p53 and inactive p53 by causing cell cycle arrest in G1 and G2/M arrest, respectively (Ma et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: NPRL2 induces apoptosis by causing cell cycle arrest in G2/M in cells with inactive p53.
source: NPRL2 induces apoptosis and DNA damage in cells with active p53 and inactive p53 by causing cell cycle arrest in G1 and G2/M arrest, respectively (Ma et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: The majority of NSCLC patients do not respond to checkpoint blockade therapy or develop resistance after initial tumor regression.
source: The majority of patients do not respond (primary resistance) or develop resistance after initial tumor regression (acquired resistance) (Sharma et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: Tumors harboring co-mutation of KRAS and STK11/LKB1 are resistant to ICB treatment.
source: The tumors harboring co-mutation of KRAS and STK11/LKB1 (KL) subtypes are also resistant to ICB treatment and showed worse overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival PFS (PFS) in the clinic (Shire et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: The inactivated STK11 gene weakens the innate immune responses by epigenetic inhibition of stimulator of IFN genes (STING).
source: The inactivated STK11 gene was recently reported to weaken the innate immune responses by epigenetic inhibition of stimulator of IFN genes (STING) (Kitajima et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: The tumor microenvironment of ICB-resistant tumors is characterized by poor infiltration of cytotoxic immune cells and higher infiltration of myeloid-derived suppressor cells.
source: The tumor microenvironment (TME) of these resistant tumors displayed a distinct immune contexture which is characterized by poor infiltration of cytotoxic immune cells and higher infiltration of myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSC) (Tumeh et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: TUSC2 selectively augments natural killer (NK) cells and cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) activity in peripheral blood and the TME.
source: TUSC2 selectively augments natural killer (NK) cells and cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) activity in peripheral blood and the TME, induces a Th1-mediated immune response, and downregulates MDSC and regulatory T cells (Treg) (Meraz et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation to previous work.

claim: TUSC2 gene therapy synergizes with anti-PD-1 in syngeneic KRAS mutant lung cancer mouse models.
source: We also showed that TUSC2 gene therapy synergizes with anti-PD-1 in syngeneic KRAS mutant lung cancer mouse models (Meraz et al., 2018; Cao et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations to previous work.

claim: The basal level of NPRL2 expression is markedly reduced in most NSCLC cells.
source: The basal level of NPRL2 expression is markedly reduced in most NSCLC cells, as we previously reported (Ueda et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with supporting citation and validated by Western blot data in Figure 1A.

claim: Transient transfection with an NPRL2 expressing plasmid restored NPRL2 expression in H1299, A549, H358, H1975, and H23 cell lines.
source: We validated the baseline expression of NPRL2 in H1299, A549, H358, H1975, and H23 cell lines, which was found to be very low or undetectable. Transient transfection with an NPRL2 expressing plasmid restored NPRL2 expression (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by Western blot data in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The level of PD-L1 expression was increased strongly in H1299 cells after NPRL2 transfection.
source: The restoration of NPRL2 in anti-PD1 therapy resistant A549 (KRAS/STK11 mutant) and moderately anti-PD1 sensitive H1299 (p53 deleted) cell lines showed that the level of PD-L1 expression was increased strongly only in H1299, whereas no change in PD-L1 expression was found in A549 followed after NPRL2 transfection (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by Western blot data in Figure 1A.

claim: No change in PD-L1 expression was found in A549 cells after NPRL2 transfection.
source: The restoration of NPRL2 in anti-PD1 therapy resistant A549 (KRAS/STK11 mutant) and moderately anti-PD1 sensitive H1299 (p53 deleted) cell lines showed that the level of PD-L1 expression was increased strongly only in H1299, whereas no change in PD-L1 expression was found in A549 followed after NPRL2 transfection (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by Western blot data in Figure 1A.

claim: Re-expression of NPRL2 strongly inhibited colony formation in both H1299 and A549 cells.
source: Re-expression of NPRL2 strongly inhibited colony formation in both H1299 and A549 cells which was statistically significant as compared with their respective empty vector (EV) transfection controls (Figure 1B) (p=0.005 in H1299; p<0.05 in A549).
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by colony formation assay data in Figure 1B-C.

claim: The degree of inhibition of colony formation in H1299 was found to be stronger than that of A549.
source: The degree of inhibition of colony formation in H1299 was found to be stronger than that of A549 (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by quantitative data in Figure 1C.

claim: NPRL2 induced apoptosis in H1299 cells with the percentage of annexin V positive cells significantly increased compared with empty vector-transfected group (37.6% in NPRL2 vs 14.5% in EV; p<0.05).
source: Scatter plots showed that after transfection of NPRL2 in H1299 cells, the percentage of annexin V positive cells was significantly increased as compared with the empty vector-transfected group (37.6% in NPRL2 vs 14.5% in EV; p<0.05) (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by flow cytometry data in Figure 1D-E.

claim: NPRL2 induced strong apoptosis in anti-PD1 resistant mouse lung cancer LLC2 cells.
source: NPRL2 also induced strong apoptosis in another anti-PD1 resistant mouse lung cancer LLC2 cells (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by flow cytometry data in Figure 1F.

claim: Humanized mice were generated by transplanting fresh human cord blood-derived CD34 stem cells into sub-lethally irradiated NSG mice.
source: Humanized mice were generated by transplanting fresh human cord blood-derived CD34 stem cells into sub-lethally irradiated NSG mice (Meraz et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the results with supporting citation to previous methodology.

claim: Mice harboring >25% human CD45 cells were considered humanized.
source: Mice harboring >25% human CD45 cells were considered humanized.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a criterion for humanization.

claim: The percentage of change in tumor intensity between pre-and post-treatment was significantly different in the NPRL2 treated group vs control in non-humanized mice (p<0.04).
source: The percentage of change in tumor intensity between pre-and post-treatment was significantly different in the NPRL2 treated group vs control (Figure 2C; p<0.04).
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by quantitative data in Figure 2C.

claim: A significantly low tumor burden was found in the percentage of change in tumor intensity between pre- vs post-treatment in the NPRL2 treatment group as compared with the empty vector group in humanized mice (p=0.003).
source: A significantly low tumor burden was found in the percentage of change in tumor intensity between pre- vs post-treatment in the NPRL2 treatment group as compared with the empty vector group (p=0.003 Figure 2G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by quantitative data in Figure 2G.

claim: The antitumor effect of NPRL2 was significantly greater in humanized mice as compared with that of non-humanized mice (p=0.008).
source: When comparing the antitumor activity between humanized and non-humanized mice, the antitumor effect of NPRL2 was significantly greater in humanized mice as compared with that of non-humanized mice (p=0.008; Figure 2H) suggesting that the immune response played a role in inducing antitumor activity.
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by comparative data in Figure 2H.

claim: The immune response played a role in inducing antitumor activity of NPRL2.
source: When comparing the antitumor activity between humanized and non-humanized mice, the antitumor effect of NPRL2 was significantly greater in humanized mice as compared with that of non-humanized mice (p=0.008; Figure 2H) suggesting that the immune response played a role in inducing antitumor activity.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison between humanized and non-humanized mice showing greater effect in immune-competent system.

claim: Pembrolizumab did not show any antitumor effect in anti-PD1-resistant A549 tumors in humanized mice.
source: Pembrolizumab did not show any antitumor effect in these anti-PD1-resistant tumors.
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by tumor growth data in Figure 2I-J.

claim: No synergistic antitumor activity was found in the NPRL2 plus pembrolizumab combination in A549 tumors.
source: No synergistic antitumor activity was found in the NPRL2 plus pembrolizumab combination.
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by tumor growth data in Figure 2I-J.

claim: 7 out of 10 mice contained an extremely low amount of tumor burden in the NPRL2 treatment group.
source: Bioluminescence imaging on mice showed that 7 out of 10 mice contained an extremely low amount of tumor burden in the NPRL2 treatment group, which was completely and visually different than in the control or pembrolizumab group (Figure 2K).
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by bioluminescence imaging in Figure 2K.

claim: Infiltration of human CD45+ cells in tumors was significantly increased in NPRL2 and NPRL2 + Pembro combination groups as compared with control (p<0.005 vs control; p<0.05 vs pembrolizumab).
source: The results showed that infiltration of human CD45+ cells in tumors was significantly increased in NPRL2 and NPRL2 + Pembro combination groups as compared with control (p<0.005 vs control; p<0.05 vs pembrolizumab; Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by flow cytometry data in Figure 3A.

claim: The percentage of human CD3+ T cells was increased by both pembrolizumab (p<0.05 vs Control) and NPRL2 treatment (p<0.0005 vs Control).
source: The percentage of human CD3+ T (p<0.05 pembrolizumab vs Control; p<0.0005 NPRL2 vs Control) and cytotoxic T cells (p<0.05 Pembrolizumab vs Control; p<0.005 NPRL2 vs Control) were increased by both pembrolizumab and NPRL2 treatment (Figure 3B–C)
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by flow cytometry data in Figure 3B.

claim: The level of TILs was significantly increased in NPRL2 treatment as compared with pembrolizumab (p<0.05 vs pembrolizumab).
source: whereas the level of TILs was significantly increased in NPRL2 treatment as compared with pembrolizumab (p<0.05 vs pembrolizumab; Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by flow cytometry data in Figure 3B.

claim: Regulatory T cells were significantly inhibited by NPRL2 treatment (p<0.005 vs control).
source: Regulatory T cells were significantly inhibited by NPRL2 treatment (p<0.005 vs control)
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by flow cytometry data in Figure 3D.

claim: The percentage of NK cells was increased by both NPRL2 alone and combination treatment (p<0.0005 control vs NPRL2).
source: whereas the percentage of NK cells was increased by both NPRL2 alone and combination treatment (Figure 3D–E; p<0.0005 control vs NPRL2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by flow cytometry data in Figure 3E.

claim: The number of activated T cells (CD69+CD8+T) was significantly increased by NPRL2 treatment (p<0.005).
source: The number of activated T cells (CD69+CD8+T) (p<0.005), effector (EM) (p<0.005), and central memory (CM) (p<0.005) CD8+ T cells were also significantly increased by NPRL2 treatment (Figure 3F–)
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by flow cytometry data in Figure 3F.

claim: Effector memory (EM) CD8+ T cells were significantly increased by NPRL2 treatment (p<0.005).
source: The number of activated T cells (CD69+CD8+T) (p<0.005), effector (EM) (p<0.005), and central memory (CM) (p<0.005) CD8+ T cells were also significantly increased by NPRL2 treatment (Figure 3F–)
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by flow cytometry data in Figure 3H.

claim: Central memory (CM) CD8+ T cells were significantly increased by NPRL2 treatment (p<0.005).
source: The number of activated T cells (CD69+CD8+T) (p<0.005), effector (EM) (p<0.005), and central memory (CM) (p<0.005) CD8+ T cells were also significantly increased by NPRL2 treatment (Figure 3F–)
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by flow cytometry data in Figure 3I.

claim: Significantly higher number of EM and CM CD8+ T cells were found after NPRL2 treatment compared with pembrolizumab (P<0.05).
source: However, as compared with pembrolizumab, significantly higher number of EM and CM CD8+ T cells were found after NPRL2 treatment (Figure 3H–I; P<0.05).
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by flow cytometry data in Figure 3H-I.

claim: The percentage of tissue-resident memory T cells (CD103+CD8+ T) was increased by NPRL2 (P<0.005 vs control, p<0.05 vs pembrolizumab).
source: The percentage of tissue-resident memory T cells (CD103+CD8+ T) was also increased by NPRL2 (Figure 3J; P<0.005 vs control, p<0.05 vs pembrolizumab).
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by flow cytometry data in Figure 3J.

claim: PD-1 expression on CD8+ T cells was drastically inhibited by pembrolizumab (p<0.00005 vs control) and combination (p<0.0005 vs control) treatment.
source: PD-1 expression on CD8+ T cells was drastically inhibited by pembrolizumab (p<0.00005 vs control) and combination (p<0.0005 vs control) treatment, whereas limited downregulation of PD-1 expression on T cells was seen in NPRL2 alone treatment (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by flow cytometry data in Figure 3G.

claim: Limited downregulation of PD-1 expression on T cells was seen in NPRL2 alone treatment.
source: PD-1 expression on CD8+ T cells was drastically inhibited by pembrolizumab (p<0.00005 vs control) and combination (p<0.0005 vs control) treatment, whereas limited downregulation of PD-1 expression on T cells was seen in NPRL2 alone treatment (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by flow cytometry data in Figure 3G.

claim: Antigen-presenting HLA-DR+ DC was significantly increased by NPRL2 (p<0.005 vs control).
source: Antigen-presenting HLA-DR+ DC (p<0.005 vs control; Figure 3K) and M1 macrophages (p<0.005 vs control; Figure 3M) were significantly increased and CD33+ MDSC cells were significantly decreased by NPRL2 (p<0.0005 vs control; Figure 3L).
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by flow cytometry data in Figure 3K.

claim: M1 macrophages were significantly increased by NPRL2 (p<0.005 vs control).
source: Antigen-presenting HLA-DR+ DC (p<0.005 vs control; Figure 3K) and M1 macrophages (p<0.005 vs control; Figure 3M) were significantly increased and CD33+ MDSC cells were significantly decreased by NPRL2 (p<0.0005 vs control; Figure 3L).
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by flow cytometry data in Figure 3M.

claim: CD33+ MDSC cells were significantly decreased by NPRL2 (p<0.0005 vs control).
source: Antigen-presenting HLA-DR+ DC (p<0.005 vs control; Figure 3K) and M1 macrophages (p<0.005 vs control; Figure 3M) were significantly increased and CD33+ MDSC cells were significantly decreased by NPRL2 (p<0.0005 vs control; Figure 3L).
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by flow cytometry data in Figure 3L.

claim: NPRL2 and pembrolizumab both showed strong antitumor effects in H1299 tumors in humanized mice.
source: NPRL2 and pembrolizumab both showed strong antitumor effects, which were statistically significant, whereas a robust and synergistic antitumor effect was observed when NPRL2 was combined with anti-PD1 immunotherapy (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by tumor growth data in Figure 4D.

claim: A robust and synergistic antitumor effect was observed when NPRL2 was combined with anti-PD1 immunotherapy in H1299 tumors.
source: NPRL2 and pembrolizumab both showed strong antitumor effects, which were statistically significant, whereas a robust and synergistic antitumor effect was observed when NPRL2 was combined with anti-PD1 immunotherapy (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by tumor growth data in Figure 4D.

claim: The percentage of cytotoxic CD8+ T and NK cells was significantly increased by the NPRL2 alone and NPRL2 +pembrolizumab combination treatment in H1299 tumors (p<0.05 vs control).
source: However, the percentage of cytotoxic CD8+ T and NK cells was significantly increased by the NPRL2 alone and NPRL2 +pembrolizumab combination treatment (p<0.05 vs control) (Figure 4F–G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by flow cytometry data in Figure 4F-G.

claim: An increased number of CD69+ activated CD8+ T cells were found in the pembrolizumab and combination groups in H1299 tumors (p<0.05 vs control).
source: An increased number of CD69+ activated CD8+ T cells were found in the pembrolizumab and combination groups (p<0.05 vs control; Figure 4I)
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by flow cytometry data in Figure 4I.

claim: The level of PD1 expression on CD8+ T was significantly downregulated by pembrolizumab, NPRL2, and combination treatments in H1299 tumors (p<0.005 vs control).
source: whereas the level of PD1 expression on CD8+ T was significantly downregulated by pembrolizumab, NPRL2, and combination treatments (p<0.005 vs control; Figure 4J).
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by flow cytometry data in Figure 4J.

claim: The number of CD103+ residential memory T cells was increased in pembrolizumab treatment in H1299 tumors (p<0.05 vs control).
source: The number of CD103+ residential memory T cells was increased in pembrolizumab treatment (p<0.05 vs control), where the number remained unaffected by NPRL2 (Figure 4K).
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by flow cytometry data in Figure 4K.

claim: The percentage of HLA-DR+ DC in the TME was significantly altered by the treatments as compared with control in H1299 tumors (p<0.05 vs pembrolizumab; p<0.005 vs NPRL2; p<0.005 vs comb).
source: The percentage of HLA-DR+ DC in the TME was significantly altered by the treatments as compared with control (p<0.05 vs pembrolizumab; p<0.005 vs NPRL2; p<0.005 vs comb; Figure 4H).
evidence: This is stated in the results and demonstrated by flow cytometry data in Figure 4H.

claim: LLC2 syngeneic tumors which have an activating KRASG12C mutation and low PD-L1 expression, are resistant to anti-PD1 checkpoint blockade.
source: LLC2 syngeneic tumors which have an activating KRASG12C mutation and low PD-L1 expression, are resistant to anti-PD1 checkpoint blockade (Li et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the results with supporting citation.
